## General Summary

The document is a three-page research packet from Bulacan Polytechnic College concerning **“EcoLegis: Legislative Document Management & AI Summary System.”** It provides English and Filipino informed-consent forms and a formal request for permission to conduct research with students and Guidance Office personnel.

The proposed study aims to evaluate the system’s functionality, usability, usefulness, and effectiveness. The packet emphasizes informed participation, confidentiality, anonymity, privacy, the right to withdraw without penalty, and the absence of foreseeable risks. Participants may also review interview transcripts, validate the study results, and suggest improvements. The final page contains the permission letter addressed to the BPC Guidance Office, along with signatures from the researchers, research adviser, and Office of the Vice President for Research and Extension.

## Page Range Breakdown

### Pages 1-2

These pages contain parallel **informed-consent forms** in English and Filipino, identified as ORE documents **ORE-2026-04** and **ORE-2026-05**. They explain the study’s nature and purpose, why participants were selected, potential benefits and risks, and their rights to ask questions, skip questions, or end participation without explanation.

Both forms assure participants that their responses and identities will remain confidential and that interviews will be recorded. Participants will receive printed transcripts for review and may amend their explanations. They may also be contacted later to validate findings and recommend improvements. The forms include partially filled respondent details and signature fields, as well as a reminder to obtain the ORE’s signature before conducting the research.

### Page 3

This page presents a formal letter dated **September 25, 2026**, from fourth-year BS Information Systems students to **Mrs. Ma. Jessica R. Quiambao**, RGC, LPT, of the Bulacan Polytechnic College Guidance Office. The students request permission to conduct the EcoLegis study at the college.

Participants will include students enrolled for **A.Y. 2026-2027**, who will evaluate the system during vacant class periods, and Guidance Office personnel, who will assess its guidance and counseling-related features. Written or verbal consent will be obtained, and all identities and responses will be anonymized and kept confidential unless expressly stated otherwise. The letter assures participants that they will receive no advantage or penalty, may withdraw without consequence, and face no foreseeable risks. It also states that anonymous research data may be preserved for reuse by other researchers.

The page ends with the signatures of the student researchers, the research adviser **Joana Marie Cruz**, and the endorsement of **Jene T. Sotto, PhD., LPT**, from the Office of the Vice President for Research and Extension.
